MO.name: Missouri
MO.instrument: Certificate of purchase, then collector's deed
MO.headline: up to 10% a year, and it depends which offering
MO.redemption: 1 year on a first or second offering; 90 days from the notice on a third; none after that
MO.note: Missouri runs the same sale up to four times and the deal changes each time. The City of St. Louis is not under this chapter at all.
rules: Counties sell under Chapter 140. The sale opens at 10:00am on the fourth Monday in August and runs day to day until every parcel has been offered (RSMo 140.150, 140.170, 140.190).
First and second offerings: bidding starts at the taxes, penalties, interest and costs. You get a certificate of purchase, not a deed, and the owner has one year to redeem (RSMo 140.290, 140.340).
Third offering: still no less than the taxes owed, but redemption drops to 90 days from the postmark on the notice of right to redeem — roughly 135 days after the sale (RSMo 140.250).

After a third offering, a post-third sale gives you the collector's deed immediately and there is NO period of redemption (RSMo 140.250.4). That is a different instrument from the first three and should be underwritten as a purchase.
Redemption pays the purchase money plus interest at a rate not exceeding 10% a year (RSMo 140.340).

Before any deed on a first, second or third offering you must get a title search report from a licensed attorney or title company, and on a third offering notify every recorded lienholder within 45 days that they have 90 days to redeem (RSMo 140.405). Post-third sales are exempt from that.
A collector's deed does NOT convey clear title. Deeds of trust, mortgages, judgments and other recorded liens survive the sale — you are taking the property with everything attached to it.
Fail to pay your bid and you owe a 25% penalty on the bid amount plus a prosecuting attorney fee (RSMo 140.280).
Non-residents of Missouri must file a Designation of Resident Agent, and the agent must accept, before bidding.

The City of St. Louis does not use Chapter 140. It runs a judicial process under the Municipal Land Reutilization Law (RSMo 92.700), where the Sheriff sells the property, a court confirmation hearing follows, and once confirmed there is no redemption at all.

MT.name: Montana
MT.headline: 10% per year (5/6 of 1% per month) plus a 2% penalty
MT.redemption: 3 years from attachment before a tax deed may be applied for
MT.note: Montana does not run a competitive bid. The county attaches the lien and holds it; any person may take an assignment by paying the delinquency, but only after mailing notice to the assessed owner — not earlier than August 15, at least two weeks before payment, and within 60 days of the assignment. The rate is statutory, so nothing is bid away. Before a deed, the assignee must notify every interested party within a window around the redemption expiry.

FL.name: Florida
FL.headline: 18% maximum, bid down
rules: Maximum interest on a certificate is 18% per year, calculated from the first day of each month (Fla. Stat. 197.172).

If interest earned at redemption is under 5% of face, a mandatory minimum of 5% applies — the redeeming party pays the certificate rate or 5%, whichever is greater. This does not apply to certificates bid at 0% (Fla. Stat. 197.472(2)).
The tax collector takes a $6.25 fee on each certificate redeemed (Fla. Stat. 197.472(3)).

CO.name: Colorado
CO.headline: 9 points over the federal discount rate
CO.stale: Rate shown is the one effective October 1, 2025. The rate for sales after October 1, 2026 is set from the federal discount rate on September 1, 2026 and must be confirmed with the State Bank Commissioner before you bid.
rules: Redemption interest is nine percentage points above the federal discount rate as of September 1, rounded to the nearest full percent, effective October 1 (C.R.S. 39-12-103(3)).
The rate set for the period beginning October 1, 2025 is 14%, from a 4.5% discount rate (State Bank Commissioner memo, Sept 2, 2025).
Your certificate keeps its rate for as long as you hold it.
Premium bid above the lien amount is never returned and earns no interest. Treat it as a cost of acquiring the lien.
Subsequent taxes you endorse onto the certificate earn the same redemption rate (C.R.S. 39-12-103).

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.headline: 15% per year plus a 3% penalty
WY.redemption: 4 years before deed application, 6 year outside limit
rules: The purchaser earns 15% simple interest per year from the date of sale, plus a 3% penalty on the amount purchased in the first year.
Subsequent taxes are optional. If you pay them they attach to the original lien and earn the same 15%.
A deed application can be made no earlier than four years from the sale, after statutory notice, and no deed can issue after six years.
Sales are typically held in person in late July or August.

sources.title: Wyo. Stat. 39-13-108 — enforcement, sale and redemption
County treasurer sale pages (Campbell, Laramie, Goshen, Sweetwater)

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.headline: 16% maximum, bid down
rules: Delinquent taxes bear 16% per year simple interest; a fraction of a month counts as a whole month (A.R.S. 42-18053).
The lien goes to the bidder accepting the lowest interest rate, and bears that bid rate from the first day of the month after purchase (A.R.S. 42-18114).
There is no minimum-interest backstop like Florida's, so a low bid is exactly what you earn.
Sales are held in February. After three years the holder may bring a judicial foreclosure (A.R.S. 42-18201).

sources.title: A.R.S. 42-18053 — interest on delinquent taxes
A.R.S. 42-18114 — lowest rate bid wins

IA.name: Iowa
IA.headline: 2% per month — 24% per year
IA.redemption: 1 year 9 months before notice of expiration
rules: The sale is the third Monday in June statewide (Iowa Code 446.7). A treasurer may move it to another June date for good cause, so the county's own notice governs the date.

Subsequent taxes may be paid one month and fourteen days after an installment goes delinquent, and accrue at the same 2% a month from the date paid. The treasurer sends no reminder, and failing to pay them can put the parcel back into the next sale.

Counties carry two kinds of leftover stock: adjourned-sale parcels nobody bid on, and public-bidder parcels advertised two years that the county now holds the certificate on. These are bought from the county, often through different offices.
Redemption requires the amount sold plus 2% per month, counting each fraction of a month as a whole month (Iowa Code 447.1).
Subsequent taxes paid by the holder earn the same 2% per month from the month of payment.
Because partial months count in full, a redemption on the first day of a month costs the same as one on the last — short holds pay disproportionately well.
The certificate holder must serve statutory notice on every party of record; only those noticed may redeem (Iowa Code 447.9).

sources.title: Iowa Code 447.1 — redemption amount, 2% per month
Iowa Code 447.9 — notice of expiration of right of redemption

IL.name: Illinois
IL.headline: 9% per six months maximum, bid down
IL.stale: Illinois is mid-reform. The 2025 sale was paused and a 2026 overhaul passed in June 2026. Confirm the current year's terms before relying on any of this.
rules: Maximum bid is 9% per six-month period, awarded to the lowest bidder; several counties report typical winning bids of 0–4% (DuPage).
Sales are in person (or sealed USB submissions under RAMS 2) with statutory costs of roughly $104–$123 per parcel paid the day of or after the sale.
Unsold parcels go to the county as trustee at 9%; DuPage states no over-the-counter forfeitures are available after the sale.
Reform legislation passed June 2026 to protect homeowner equity; the interest structure and procedures may change for coming sales.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.instrument: Tax lien certificate (new system effective Jan 1, 2026)
LA.headline: 1% per month, bid down to a 0.7% floor, plus 5% penalty
LA.redemption: 3 years, then judicial foreclosure with surplus to the owner
rules: From January 1, 2026 Louisiana sells tax lien certificates instead of fractional 'tax sale title'. Sales before that date stay under the old law.
Bidding starts at 1% per month and moves in 0.1% steps to a floor of 0.7% per month (8.4% per year); lowest rate wins, first-to-bid breaks ties — only four bid positions exist.
Redemption pays the taxes, a fixed 5% penalty, and the auction interest; after three years the holder brings a court-supervised foreclosure and any surplus goes to the former owner.
Certificates not purchased at auction are held by the political subdivision; a seven-year limit runs from recording to enforce an unredeemed certificate.

sources.title: La. R.S. 47:2156 (eff. Jan 1, 2026 on ratification of Act 409)
Louisiana Law Help — tax sales after 2026
Act 557 / Act 774 summaries (adjudicated property and lien overhaul)

TX.name: Texas
TX.headline: 25% redemption premium; 180 days (2 years homestead/ag)
TX.redemption: 180 days for most property; 2 years for homestead, agricultural and mineral interests
rules: The purchaser receives a deed and the right of possession during the redemption period (Tex. Tax Code 34.21).
Non-homestead property: the former owner may redeem within 180 days of the deed being filed for record, paying a premium capped at 25%.
Homestead and agricultural property: two years, with a 25% premium in year one and 50% in year two, on the bid, deed fee, and taxes and costs paid.
Sources disagree on whether the clock starts at the sale or when the deed is recorded — the statute says when the purchaser's deed is filed for record.

sources.title: Tex. Tax Code 34.21 — right of redemption
Hill County Tax Office — tax sale

ID.name: Idaho
ID.headline: No stated rate — deed state
rules: Idaho conveys by tax deed rather than selling certificates, so there is no statutory investor rate to compute. Return is resale spread.
The statutory process, notice requirements, and the county's sale terms have NOT been verified here. Do not rely on this card for Idaho procedure.

facts.label: Sale timing
facts.value: Online, early February each year; auction site opens mid-January for research and registration (Jan 16 for the 2026 cycle)

facts.label: Deposit
facts.value: 10% of the amount you intend to purchase, by ACH debit on the auction site; minimum $500; can be raised until the auction closes

facts.label: Registration
facts.value: W-9 (or W-8BEN) and SSN/TIN per bidder; bidder number takes 24–48 hours to reach the Treasurer

facts.label: Bid method
facts.value: Rate bid down from 16% in 1% increments; lowest accepted rate wins

facts.label: Subsequent taxes
facts.value: Sub-tax window June 1 – December 31, $5 fee, earns the same rate as the original certificate

facts.label: Advertising
facts.value: Arizona Business Gazette, about three weeks before the sale; advertising list also sold as an FTP file for $25

facts.label: OTC
facts.value: State assignments purchasable year-round; tax-deeded land offered over the counter after an unsold auction

links.label: Park County — County-Held Tax Lien Certificates

facts.label: Interest or penalty
facts.value: 9 points over the federal discount rate
facts.caveat: Rate shown is the one effective October 1, 2025. The rate for sales after October 1, 2026 is set from the federal discount rate on September 1, 2026 and must be confirmed with the State Bank Commissioner before you bid.

facts.label: OTC
facts.value: County-held certificates: certificate value plus $4 assignment fee, cash or certified funds, W-9 required

facts.label: Deed path
facts.value: Treasurer's deed application after 3 years; $1,000 application fee; 7–9 months

facts.label: Restriction
facts.value: County employees and families may not purchase

facts.label: Auction type
facts.value: Tax lien certificate. The page says you do not have an ownership right, only a property tax lien, until you apply for and receive a deed.

facts.label: Interest or penalty
facts.value: 13% for 2026 certificates. The page says redeemed certificates pay nine points over the federal discount rate.
facts.caveat: A September 2026 research note and an October 8, 2026 page scrape both recorded October 16, 2026 as the sale date, and the research note recorded a 15% rate. The treasurer page opened November 12, 2026 says November 6, 2026 and 13%. The October 16 date is not shown as current.

facts.label: Redemption period
facts.value: The page says you may apply after 3 years. Premiums are not returned and do not draw interest.

facts.label: Platform
facts.value: RealAuction. Batches of about 400 properties close in one-hour steps, with batch 1 closing at 9:00 a.m. MDT.

facts.label: Auction date
facts.value: The Mesa County tax lien sale will be held via the internet on November 6, 2026. Research on the auction site was scheduled to begin Monday, September 21, 2026.
facts.caveat: A September 2026 research note and an October 8, 2026 page scrape both recorded October 16, 2026 as the sale date, and the research note recorded a 15% rate. The treasurer page opened November 12, 2026 says November 6, 2026 and 13%. The October 16 date is not shown as current.

facts.label: Registration deadline
facts.value: Registration and a deposit are required before a bid is accepted. The page says deposits have a due date and tells the reader to check the schedule of events. It does not print that due date in the bidding section.

facts.label: Deposit
facts.value: 10% of the dollar amount of certificates the bidder anticipates winning, by ACH inside RealAuction, no later than 2:00 p.m. on the deposit due date. Personal checks and cash are not accepted for the deposit. Winning bids must be paid on the auction site no later than November 9, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. MDT.

facts.label: Payment deadline
facts.value: Winning bidders must pay the auction site no later than November 9, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. MDT.

facts.label: From the county page
facts.value: Premium bidding above 30% shows a warning the bidder can pass. Premiums are a cost of the lien and are not returned.

facts.label: From the county page
facts.value: County employees, officials, their immediate families, and agents may not acquire a lien (C.R.S. 39-11-151).

facts.label: Conflict in the county file
facts.value: Mesa's page states 15% for the current sale while the Bank Commissioner's published rate effective October 1, 2025 is 14%. One of the two is out of date. Confirm with the treasurer before bidding.
facts.caveat: Recorded in September 2026. The page opened November 12, 2026 is the later reading.

facts.label: Bid method
facts.value: Premium bid at bidder discretion up to 30%; above 30% triggers a warning you can click past
